facts.text: My right ring finger is swollen.

facts.item: worsening of the finger pain and swelling
facts.text: The swelling and the pain have been getting worse.
The pain and swelling started 2 days ago, while I was playing football.
My finger got caught in another player's jersey, and he pulled away forcefully.
The pain is at the last joint of the finger, the one nearest the fingertip.

facts.item: difficulty bending the tip of the finger
facts.text: When I make a fist, I can't bend my right ring finger at the last joint.
When my hand is resting, my right ring finger stays straight.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
I'm active in sports, especially football.
I don't have any tingling in the finger.

findings.name: hand examination
findings.result: Inspection: right ring finger extended, with visible swelling at the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint; palpation: tenderness localized to the DIP joint of the right ring finger; range of motion: unable to flex the right ring finger at the DIP joint when attempting to make a fist; no joint laxity.

findings.name: neurovascular examination of the hand
findings.result: Normal capillary refill; no sensory deficits.

findings.name: X-ray of the right hand
findings.result: No fractures or dislocations. Soft tissue swelling around the DIP joint of the right ring finger.

gold.diagnosis: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
aliases: avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon
FDP tendon avulsion from the distal phalanx
FDP tendon rupture at its insertion

No joint laxity.

x008: The source's 'Preliminary_Findings' only says what the MRI is expected to show; it gives no result. The MRI is listed as obtained, so the record exists with 'Result not documented'.

source_issues: The MRI leaf contains an expectation ('Expected to show details regarding the integrity of tendons') rather than a finding.
notes: The chief complaint names two complaints (swelling, pain), so both open the case; 'progressive' applies to both and is a standalone fact (f003), as are the onset during football (f004) and the jersey mechanism (f005).
'Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint' (p003) is the location child of the finger pain, in lay words (last joint, nearest the fingertip).
The hand inspection, palpation and range of motion form one hand-examination record; the neurovascular assessment is a separate request.
No finding name or alias uses a gold term (flexor, profundus, tendon).

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger.
